artifacts.summary: Empirically confirms $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is exported to hook commands (both event types and the nested bash -c shape) and demonstrates the fixed form still blocks a real guard; maps the root-files/merge-sources dedup overlap, rules out the settings.local.json permission matchers as out of scope, and rules in favor of an explicit migration script for already-deployed repos.

memory_candidates.content: Claude Code exports $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR into hook command environments (confirmed for PreToolUse:Bash and PostToolUse:Write, including inside a nested `bash -c '...'` wrapper) resolved to the true project/repo root, independent of the session's Bash-tool CWD. It is ABSENT from the Bash tool's own command execution environment -- only the hook-launching mechanism injects it. Use `bash "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/hooks/x.sh` for any hook registration instead of a bare `bash .claude/hooks/x.sh`, which silently fails open (exit 127, non-blocking) once the session cwd drifts into a subdirectory.

In this repo's extension deploy model, deep_merge dedup (merge.lua) matches hook entries by exact vim.deep_equal on the whole hook object including its command string. root-files/settings.json is install-once (copied only on first install, never overwritten by resync) while merge-sources/*.json propagate on every resync. When a hook's command string changes, any hook that exists identically in BOTH a merge-source and an already-deployed (install-once-sourced) settings.json must be rewritten identically in both places, or the next resync appends a duplicate entry under the same matcher rather than replacing the stale one -- deep_merge cannot self-heal a changed/renamed command string. This is pre-existing, documented behavior (core/manifest.json's merge_targets.settings _comment), not unique to one task.
